implementation_state: The store holds the canonical OutcomeTrainingSample, and production ingestion runs exactly once per eligible request as the last step of the single terminal transition, fed by the request's own retained decision-time input and its one validated Outcome. Refusal is explicit and counted, retention is bounded by count and age with counted evictions, non-success terminal states survive with their failure class, and no dataset condition can fail a request. Accepted on dev at 5e3f49b.
unblock_condition: Accepted: canonical storage, once-per-request validated ingestion, observable refusal, count-and-age retention, and intact non-success terminal states are all proven.
notes: The audit kept this node blocked for want of a trustworthy production Outcome; that reason is closed and the node's own work is accepted.

KNOWN LIMITATION, recorded rather than hidden: the sample features come from a snapshot cloned at decision time on the path where the shadow record was accepted, not from a re-read of that record. The values are identical and nothing is re-derived, but the authority is the lifecycle copy. The store needs a read accessor such as ShadowStore::retained_input(request_id) to make the correlation authoritative; adding it is a one-line swap at the call site and is the named follow-up.
The worker refused the only existing alternative, ShadowStore::decisions(), because it clones the whole retained window and would put an O(n) clone on the request terminal path.

Dataset collection currently follows config.shadow.enabled, because no dataset-specific configuration exists and inventing a second switch would imply a second feature source. Collection is therefore off wherever shadow recording is off.
The Outcome is cloned once per request so the activity log and the dataset can each own one; the dataset ring is in-process and bounded, with no disk persistence.
Accepted as 597f553 on node/7b-dataset, integrated as 5e3f49b; review and gates are E-070 through E-072.
